questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was important to me that I could see myself live in the city and could be speak the language fluently.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My study abroad has involved more than the academic aspect. The everyday life when moving to a new place has been so interesting to adapt into. The culture at the hospital is very different from home, even though it is Australia. But the placement is comparable to Denmark - but with less hands on time.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I figured out who had been abroad at the same hospital through network at home - and they were a big help in this process. It can feel like the information is sparse and you really want to confirm that you do not miss a deadline. When I first got received an e-mail from the host university, everything was better.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was in contact with the education manager and could reach out to him at any time. He showed my around the first day of arrival.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found it through Airbnb and it is very expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is expensive but worth to life near centrum (Surry hills, redfern, Waterloo)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
The registration process takes a lot of time and it is difficult to figure out the necessary steps. You have to fill out a lot of health papers and retake some blood test at home prior to arrival to confirm your health. This proces is comprehensive!
The process of choosing the departments of your placement is alright. You just write your wishes to the education manager and then he replies if they are manageable.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I had wished for more information from every department.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I did wish for pediatric, but there is no such department at Concord Hospital. But otherwise it was fine.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is very difficult to know in advance how the departments involve the medical students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore every part of Sydney. It is big and great and has many fun things to do. Go to Melbourne and drive the great ocean road.

questions.answer: The weather, the mornings, the active people

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Sydney is the best city to move to. 
Do not expect to meet new friends at the hospital 
Use a lot of time to explore the city and outside areas
